summary: The paper benchmarks sparse boundary inference and witness selection policies on a simulated 192³ cellular memory grid under translated spatial faults. The experimental design rigorously isolates boundary from witness sampling, demonstrating that sampling under 1% of the field incurs only a 0.31 percentage point deficit compared to full observation while maintaining a 6.25 point advantage over fixed geometry. The benchmark documentation is mathematically sound and specifies detailed hardware and execution parameters, though the condensed prose requires domain familiarity.
strengths: Rigorous ablation design that isolates the effect of boundary inference from witness selection across matched control arms.
Comprehensive statistical reporting including paired deficit confidence intervals and false write tracking.
Exact mathematical consistency in sampling bounds, grid calculations, and percentage shifts.
Detailed runtime environment documentation with concrete execution receipts and hardware specifications.
weaknesses: Dense and telegraphic writing style that assumes extensive prior familiarity with the underlying spatial memory simulation architecture.
Lacks an end-to-end discussion of hardware timing overheads and actual wall-clock throughput tradeoffs beyond simulated tick counts.
Submitted as text-only without direct platform-level repository binding, limiting immediate automated pipeline verification.
suggestions: Expand the introductory context describing the underlying cellular automata/memory architecture and the operational mechanics of the seven update commands.
Incorporate runtime execution overheads comparing the CPU/GPU time spent computing sparse sampling versus dense aggregation.
Provide visual diagrams clarifying the spatial arrangement of the 64 detector lines and the 1,024 regional anchor offsets.

claims.text: At 192³, the upper bound on scalar readings consulted in the sampled decision is 3 × 64 × 192 + 4 × 8 × 1024 = 69,632 of 7,077,888, which uses at most 0.984% of the field as input.
The equivalent upper fraction at 96³ was 5.79%.
Environment capture from the Studio records arm64 Apple M5 Ultra and 256 GiB memory, macOS build 26B118, Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4 in float32 and NumPy 2.5.5.
